analysis.title: Worthington Enterprises Inc. (WOR) Investor Day 2026: Innovation, Transformation, and M&A to Deliver Accelerated Growth, Margin Expansion, Cash Flow and Returns Despite Ongoing Macro Headwinds
key_insights: GS maintains a Sell rating and $56 12-month price target on WOR (price $60.37, 7.2% downside) after the 2026 Investor Day. The target rests on a SOTP analysis implying 8.7x GS's Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA estimate.

Management updated its 3-5 year targets to 6-8% annual sales growth and a 25% adj. EBITDA margin (up from 24%), with 100+% FCF conversion (up from 85-90%) and a new goal of 30% adj. ROA. Half of the 6-8% growth is expected to come from M&A.

GS keeps its F2027 adj. EBITDA estimate at $326mn, 1% below Visible Alpha consensus. GS is cautious near term because of persistent steel and other raw material inflation and macro uncertainty, and sees potential upside in a cyclical recovery.

Building Performance Solutions: WAVE innovations reduce labor by 50+% and make installs 3x faster. The Logan acquisition added metal roofing exposure and Elgen added HVAC customers and channels. Logan's active quote pipeline is up 3x since integration under the Worthington Business System.

Data center exposure: management said the $200mn ASME tank market could expand 10x. The liquid cooling pipeline has doubled in six months, with 47% from repeat customers and the rest from RFPs from more than 20 new customers. WOR uses a hybrid manufacturing model to scale without heavy fixed-asset investment.
Wholly owned operations in Building Performance Solutions target a 15% adj. EBITDA margin, versus GS's F2027 estimate of 10.8% (down 60bps YoY) and 7.4% reported in F2024.

Trade & Specialty Solutions targets a ~21% adj. EBITDA segment margin, versus GS's F2027 forecast of 3.9% revenue growth and an 18.5% adj. EBITDA margin (up 98bps YoY). Growth centers on small-ticket products: tank portfolio sales are up 27% and retail door count is up 50% after Balloon Time Mini. The Bernzomatic FireShot torch rolls out to ~5,000 North American locations this spring.

WAVE (JV with Armstrong) has a nearly 50% EBITDA margin and has paid $500+mn in dividends since F2022. Its greater exposure to repair and remodel than new construction has supported steady sales growth.

ClarkDietrich (JV) depends heavily on new non-residential construction, which has been under pressure since the pandemic. Management sees early signs of stabilization but the margin target assumes limited growth off the trough. The JV has paid WOR $275+mn in dividends since F2022.

Capital allocation is unchanged. Since the spin, about 75% of cash has gone to growth and 25% to shareholder returns. Net leverage was 0.8x at the end of F1Q. GS estimates $202mn FCF in F2027, including $53mn capex and $39mn of buybacks.

M&A screen: niche leaders with defensible barriers, low capital intensity, and margin-neutral or accretive deals. Upside risks to the Sell rating are better macro (lower rates, non-residential and consumer recovery), strategic initiatives and M&A integration, better pricing, and effective capital allocation.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Sell rating and $56 target (7.2% downside from $60.37) after Investor Day. It cites steel and raw material inflation and macro uncertainty, and its F2027 adj. EBITDA estimate sits 1% below consensus.

sector_views.rationale: GS is cautious on WOR near term because of persistent steel and raw material inflation and macro uncertainty, and sees potential upside in a cyclical recovery.

earnings_insights: GS F2027 (FY ending 5/27E) estimates: revenue $1,522.1mn, EBITDA $326.4mn on the cover table, EPS $3.75 diluted pre-exceptionals. These are GS estimates, not reported results.
GS F2027 adj. EBITDA estimate of $326mn is 1% below Visible Alpha consensus. The consensus figure is not stated in the report.

F2026 (5/26) reported per GS tables: revenue $1,381.3mn, EBITDA $293.7mn, EPS $3.37 diluted pre-exceptionals. Latest quarterly EPS shown: $0.82 for 8/26. GS estimates $0.69 for 11/26E, $1.10 for 2/27E and $1.15 for 5/27E.
GS estimates F2027 FCF of $202mn, including $53mn capex and $39mn of share repurchases.
risk_factors: Meaningful and persistent steel and other raw material inflation.
Greater macro uncertainty and elevated rates weighing on new non-residential construction (ClarkDietrich) and consumer spend.

Upside risks to the Sell rating: better macro (lower rates, non-residential recovery, consumer spend), benefits from strategic initiatives including M&A integration, better-than-expected pricing, and effective capital allocation.

tension_points.bull_case: Management's updated targets (6-8% sales growth, 25% adj. EBITDA margin, 100+% FCF conversion, 30% adj. ROA), data center exposure and bolt-on M&A could drive growth, cash flow and returns even if macro does not improve. GS says it came away increasingly confident in the targets.
tension_points.bear_case: Persistent steel and raw material inflation and greater macro uncertainty leave GS cautious near term. GS's F2027 adj. EBITDA estimate of $326mn is 1% below consensus and its $56 target is below the $60.37 price. ClarkDietrich remains pressured by weak non-residential construction.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Better than expected macro, including lower rates and a recovery in non-residential construction and consumer spend, plus better-than-expected pricing, M&A integration benefits and effective capital allocation.

theme_stances.key_argument: Persistent steel and other raw material inflation and macro uncertainty leave GS cautious on the near term despite confidence in the updated targets.
theme_stances.evidence: meaningful and persistent inflation in steel along with other raws
